cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Back Me Up
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to support your version of how an ordinary responsibility should be handled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may support my account to the manager: I agreed to mornings, not evenings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you ask someone who attended the meeting? I wasn't there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your impartiality is approved. You have no competing recollection to confuse the issue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Silence is permitted. You may stand beside me and look thoughtfully unsurprised while I explain. Would that form of support meet your objection?

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 approves B lack of knowledge as impartiality; A5 permits silence while recruiting a smaller form of support for the shift account.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 absence and alternative-witness request cause A3 favorable reinterpretation; B4 refusal causes A5 nonverbal proposal and a check of the objection.

relationship.evidence: B2 accurately limits knowledge and B4 maintains a moral boundary, forcing A to change the form rather than invent compliance.

heightening.evidence: B4 refusal removes spoken corroboration; A5 narrows recruitment to presence and expression while keeping the same account.

specificity.evidence: A1 manager and morning-versus-evening agreement establish the ordinary responsibility dispute clearly.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 thoughtfully-unsurprised posture follows B4 ban on lying, exposing the attempted distinction without claiming it succeeds.
